content.intro: Learn session management through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Session Management matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines session management as part of authentication, authorization, and user accounts. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Creating sessions; Accessing session data; Session expiration; Session invalidation; Cookies and session security. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Creating sessions
items.text: Sessions associate server-side (or configured signed-cookie) state with a browser session. Use a suitable backend, expiry and secure cookie settings; avoid storing secrets or large mutable records in cookies.

items.title: Accessing session data
items.text: Accessing session data is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Session expiration
